newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ad agency says it has the key to kids.
newsitem.headline: German ad agency says it has the key to kids.

text.p: That children can be tough customers is no secret, but a German advertiser said on Monday it has made a science out of winning them over.

Advertising agency Springer & Jacoby (S & J) said it was trying out techniques to appeal to youngsters based on a study it had commissioned in adverts for Unilever's Cornetto ice cream in top German children's magazine Bravo.

The ads, which will appear in the April 10 issue of Bravo, implement findings of a two-year-long "Kids-Network" study in which S & J's research team questioned children every two weeks about their reaction to various ads.

"Kids are living increasingly in their own world. Because we as adults know less and less what is going on there, this target group proves to be consistently underestimated," said Tonio Kroeger, an S & J customer relations director.
"Kids today are a critical target group. They develop a strong market awareness very early on and have enormous buying power," Kroeger said.

S & J identified six main problems in creating successful children's ads: a heterogeneous target group, today's "shorter childhoods", mounting competition, different perception faculties, sensitive moral sensibilities and current trends.

The agency also based its study, which was released last autumn, on experience with clients which market children's products such as Virgin Interactive Entertainment and T-Mobil pagers from telecoms group Deutsche Telekom's.
S & J said it had already started applying its study's findings to campaigns for these clients.

"Cornetto" has not advertised in six years, posts a name-recognition factor of 82 percent but is not accepted by consumers between 12 and 16 years old, S & J said, conditions which made it an ideal candidate on which to test its results.
